title: SpecLoR: Improving Video Generation with Inference-Time Spectral Lookahead Rectification
claim: Sampling trajectories drift from the ideal path; a lookahead, frequency-domain correction re-anchors them to a more valid trajectory.
layout: 2 panels: manifold trajectory sketch left, circular loop diagram right; video frames inset
description: Two panels. Panel (a) shows a curved 3D surface, the video latent manifold, with a color gradient from red at the top to green at the bottom. A black ideal trajectory arcs over the surface. A blue rectified trajectory and a red baseline trajectory zigzag below it, both starting from the same point. Dashed arrows mark the rectification steps. Beside them is a green rounded text prompt about an ice hockey player. Two pairs of video frames link to the trajectories: a blue-bordered pair for the rectified result and a red-bordered pair for the baseline, with a circled artifact. Panel (b) is a cycle of nodes: z_t goes by lookahead to z_{t,0}, then 3D FFT, amplitude rectification (a noisy spectrum becomes a smooth decay curve with a green check), and 3D iFFT to ẑ_{t,0}. Re-noising gives ẑ_t, and a latent update arrow returns to z_t. Red and blue circles distinguish the original and corrected states.
caption: Concept and pipeline of \Ours. (a) Accumulated errors drift the Flow Matching trajectory from the ideal trajectory, yielding spatiotemporal inconsistencies. \Ours seamlessly anchors it back to a more valid trajectory. (b) At early timesteps, we project the noisy latent $z_t$ to a lookahead state $z_{t,0}$. We decouple its spatiotemporal spectrum, rectifying only the amplitude to a universal prior while preserving phase. The corrected state $\hat{z}_{t,0}$ is then re-noised to $\hat{z}_t$, resuming ODE integration.
abstract: Flow Matching has enabled high-fidelity text-to-video generation via latent ODE sampling. However, velocity approximation and numerical discretization errors inevitably accumulate during inference, causing sampling trajectories to drift from the intended generative path. Consequently, generated videos often suffer from severe spatiotemporal inconsistencies. A natural idea is to correct this drift during sampling, but direct intervention in the noisy latent space is challenging: (i) timestep-dependent noise obscures reliable structural cues; (ii) spatial interventions risk disrupting intricate local geometry while incurring heavy computational costs. To address these challenges, we propose Spectral Lookahead Rectification (**SpecLoR**), an inference-time method that bypasses noise via lookahead prediction, and circumvents spatiotemporal entanglement by shifting corrections to the frequency domain. First, during early sampling stages, SpecLoR estimates the clean latent $z_{t,0}$ from the current noisy state and computes its 3D spatiotemporal spectrum. Next, SpecLoR rectifies the amplitude spectrum to align with natural-video spectral statistics. Finally, the corrected state is re-noised back to the current timestep to resume ODE integration. Experiments on Wan2.2 show that SpecLoR reduces physical artifacts and enhances motion coherence across multiple benchmarks with minimal computational overhead (4 additional NFEs).
